text: Citi Pulls Back on U.S. Stocks as Trade War Clouds Outlook Muslim Farooque April 15, 2025 1 min read Citigroup ( NYSE:C ) downgraded its outlook on U.S. equities Monday , citing elevated valuations and increasing earnings risks as trade tensions escalate. The bank shifted its view from overweight to neutral, pointing to signs that the U.S. economic and earnings edge may be waning. The drivers of U.S. exceptionalism are fading, both in terms of GDP and corporate profits, analysts led by Beata Manthey wrote. They noted that current and proposed tariffs pose the greatest threat to U.S. earnings per share among global markets. According to Citi, broader structural shifts are also putting pressure on U.S. equity dominance, including growing competition from China's DeepSeek AI model and fiscal stimulus efforts in Europe. The firm observed early signs of capital rotation out of the U.S. and into international markets, reversing years of strong inflows. Despite recession concerns easing, the bank warned that risks remain. The U.S. now faces some of the steepest base tariffs in 100 years, with additional leviesincluding 10% broad tariffs and a 145% rate on Chinese goodsstill expected to weigh on global growth and lift U.S. inflation. In contrast, Citi upgraded Japan to overweight from underweight, citing its potential to avoid the brunt of U.S. trade measures. Europe remains overweight, with regional stocks viewed as already reflecting the impact of 20% U.S. tariffs and offering relatively appealing valuations. Emerging markets were downgraded to underweight, as China continues to face disproportionate tariff exposure despite recent exemptions for technology products.
